newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds focus on emerging market deals.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds focus on emerging market deals.

text.p: New issues from emerging market borrowers provided the focus during a quiet Wednesday morning Eurobond session.
Bank Handlowy launched a well-flagged $150 million three-year bond, priced to yield 60 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, via J.P. Morgan.
Officials at the lead manager were not immediately available for comment, but dealers elsewhere said the bond had been well-received, reflecting the scarcity of Polish paper.
Handlowy first came to the Eurobond market in 1996, when it issued a $100 million three-year bond at 88 b.p. over Treasuries. This was now trading between 50 and 55 b.p. over.

Some dealers said the three-year maturity on Poland's Bank Handlowy deal was "on the defensive side" because it had been eyeing a five-year maturity, but added the borrower was well-known and the paper would sell due to its rarity appeal
On the sovereign side, Argentina issued a 50 billion yen seven-year Eurobond via Yamaichi International.
The deal was targeted at Japanese institutional investors but had also seen broad-based interest from investors elsewhere, a Yamaichi syndicate official said.
"The bond gives a good yield pick up (200 basis points over Japanese LIBOR) and pays an attractive coupon of 4.40 percent," he said.
He said demand was dampened by market holidays. On Thursday many markets are on holiday for May Day celebrations.
Turning to the mark sector, Croatia added its name to the queue of emerging market borrowers due to issue bonds there.
It mandated Credit Suisse First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to lead manage its debut mark bond, but gave no details of the transaction.
Syndicate managers covering the sector said Croatia could raise up to 500 million marks with a five- to seven-year maturity. Spread was seen at 50 to 60 b.p. over Libor.
Also in the pipeline is a 300 to 500 million mark deal for Slovenia, which will be underwritten by CSFB and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
Slovenia could issue seven- to 10-year bonds, and spread talk was 25 to 35 b.p. over Libor.

Elsewhere, information released on Tuesday that the City of Moscow would launch a $400 million three-year bond sparked talk bonds by other Russian municipalities would be restricted to similar maturities.
Russia had been considering a five-year bond, but bankers said a central bank licence would limit the deal's maturity to three years.
It was unclear whether this would restrict the maturity on other Russian deals like those planned by St Petersburg and the Nizhny Novgorod region, bankers said.
